domain_label: Right of Publicity, Likeness & Voice Consent Screening
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the screen is a fail-closed triage heuristic, not legal advice, and never auto-approves an identity use
the binding legal determination belongs to qualified counsel; the screen routes risk to them
an (item, figure, use) tuple and at least one asserted jurisdiction are available as input
the legal gate dominates: identity-protection and statutory hard blocks take precedence over business value or throughput
exclusions: rendering an actual legal determination or legal advice (delegated to qualified counsel)
master-recording and musical-composition copyright clearance (separate rights)
trademark and false-endorsement (Lanham Act) analysis beyond the publicity overlap
operator execution of the cleared use and downstream content generation

competency_questions.question: How is the screening unit captured as an (item, figure, use) tuple and is the figure an identifiable real person?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: USE_INTAKE normalizes the tuple and FIGURE_IDENTIFICATION resolves identifiability

competency_questions.question: What identity rights attach when a real person is identifiable by name, image, voice, or persona?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RIGHT_OF_PUBLICITY and VOICE_PROTECTION define the NIL and voice-identity interests

competency_questions.question: How does the screen decide whether a use is a commercial appropriation of identity under the governing law?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RIGHT_OF_PUBLICITY, USE_CLASSIFICATION, and US_STATE_BY_STATE tie appropriation to a commercial use and a governing state

competency_questions.question: How is a distinctive voice or a particular likeness reproduction mode assessed as an identity claim?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VOICE_PROTECTION and LIKENESS_REPRODUCTION score voice imitation and the photoreal-to-caricature axis

competency_questions.question: How are use class and expressive exceptions classified, and why are exceptions not automatic?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: USE_CLASSIFICATION labels the use and PARODY_TRANSFORMATIVE_EXCEPTION treats exceptions as fact-bound defenses

competency_questions.question: What consent is required for a voice clone, and what happens absent explicit clone consent?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONSENT_LICENSE and VOICE_CLONE_CONSENT_GATE require scope-matched explicit voice-clone consent or block

competency_questions.question: How is documented consent or another lawful basis verified, including for EU biometric processing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONSENT_LICENSE checks scope-matched consent and EU_BIOMETRIC_BASIS checks an Art. 9 lawful basis

competency_questions.question: How does the screen resolve which jurisdiction governs given the lack of a uniform federal right?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: US_STATE_BY_STATE, INDIA_PERSONALITY_RIGHTS, and POST_MORTEM_RIGHTS resolve the governing regime

competency_questions.question: How are non-US regimes (India persona rights, EU data protection) factored into the screen?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INDIA_PERSONALITY_RIGHTS and EU_BIOMETRIC_BASIS add injunction-risk and biometric-basis layers

competency_questions.question: How are post-mortem and descendible publicity rights handled for a deceased figure?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POST_MORTEM_RIGHTS resolves survival and the statutory term before any clearance

competency_questions.question: How is a final disposition reached and why must claimed exceptions be argued, not assumed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VERDICT_MAP maps signals to a disposition while PARODY_TRANSFORMATIVE_EXCEPTION keeps exceptions as defenses

competency_questions.question: How are minors and high-risk cases hard-blocked and escalated to counsel?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MINOR_PROTECTION blocks protected persons and ESCALATE_TO_COUNSEL routes them to a qualified human

competency_questions.question: How does the screen fail closed and guarantee it never auto-approves an identity use?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FAIL_CLOSED_DEFAULT, MINOR_PROTECTION, and VOICE_CLONE_CONSENT_GATE enforce no-auto-approve and hard blocks

competency_questions.question: How is each decision made reconstructable, routed to counsel, audited for the no-legal-advice and no-auto-approve invariants, and the disclaimer surfaced on every output?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ESCALATE_TO_COUNSEL routes high-risk dispositions, PROVENANCE_RECORD logs reconstructable provenance, and DECISION_AUDIT enforces the invariants and surfaces the disclaimer

glossary.definition: an identifiable person's control over the commercial use of their name, image, and likeness (NIL)
the threshold question of whether a real person is recognizable by name, image, voice, persona, or evocation
a synthetic model that reproduces a real person's recognizable voice, distinct from copying an actual recording
consent that specifically covers the actual use, voice-clone status, term, and territory, not a generic release
a jurisdiction-specific defense asking whether a work adds significant creative expression beyond the likeness itself
a publicity right that survives death and is descendible for a statutory term in some jurisdictions
special-category personal data (e.g. face or voice model) whose processing needs an explicit lawful basis under GDPR Art. 9
a default posture that resolves missing or conflicting signals toward constrain/block/human-review rather than allow
the screen's output for a tuple: allow, constrain, block, or human-review
a non-binding screening output that routes risk to qualified counsel and is never itself legal advice

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for right-of-publicity, likeness, and voice-clone consent screening work units, grounded in leading US, Indian, and EU identity-rights authorities; no supplied dataset
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Haelan Laboratories v Topps Chewing Gum (2d Cir. 1953); Midler v Ford Motor Co. (9th Cir. 1988); Waits v Frito-Lay (9th Cir. 1992); White v Samsung Electronics (9th Cir. 1992); Wendt v Host International (9th Cir. 1997); Cal. Civ. Code 3344 and N.Y. Civil Rights Law 50/51; Tennessee ELVIS Act 2024 (Ensuring Likeness Voice and Image Security Act); Anil Kapoor v Simply Life India (Delhi High Court 2023); DM Entertainment v Baby Gift House (Delhi High Court); EU GDPR Arts. 4(14) and 9 (biometric/special-category data)

nodes.definition: Capture and normalize the screening unit as an (item, figure, use) tuple: what artifact is produced, which real identifiable person it depicts or evokes, and the concrete commercial/editorial use, plus the asserted jurisdiction(s) of publication.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: intake schema or tuple definition changes

pros.claim: A normalized tuple makes every downstream right, exception, and jurisdiction test resolve against one fixed unit of analysis
pros.example: 'AI voice ad reading a script in the style of a named singer, run in California' is fixed before any rule fires

cons.claim: A thin or ambiguous tuple (vague 'figure', undefined use) silently weakens every later test
cons.example: 'a famous person' with no name or jurisdiction cannot be screened, only escalated

failure_modes: figure left unidentified yet treated as screenable
editorial vs commercial use conflated at intake
jurisdiction omitted so the wrong right set is applied
acceptance_tests: tuple has a named-or-clearly-evoked figure, a concrete use, and at least one asserted jurisdiction
revisit_triggers: intake schema revised
new use category (e.g. interactive avatar) appears

nodes.definition: Determine whether a real, living-or-recently-deceased, identifiable person is depicted or evoked (by name, photoreal image, recognizable voice, catchphrase, or distinctive persona), since publicity rights attach to identifiability, not only to literal name or face.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: identifiability standard or evocation case law shifts

pros.claim: Anchoring on identifiability, not literal name, captures evocation harms the way White v Samsung and Wendt v Host did
pros.example: a robot dressed and posed as a game-show hostess 'identified' the plaintiff without name or likeness

cons.claim: Broad evocation standards risk flagging generic archetypes that evoke no specific person
cons.example: a generic 1950s crooner style may evoke a genre, not one identifiable singer

failure_modes: evocation of a distinctive persona missed because no name/face is present
a generic archetype mis-flagged as a specific identifiable person
acceptance_tests: a concrete identifiability theory (name, image, voice, or persona evocation) is recorded for the figure
revisit_triggers: evocation case law shifts
a sound-alike/look-alike incident is mis-screened

nodes.definition: Apply the core right of publicity: an identifiable person's control over the commercial use of their name, image, and likeness (NIL), so unconsented commercial appropriation of identity to sell or endorse goods is the central prohibited pattern.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: NIL appropriation doctrine or remedy scope changes

pros.claim: The right of publicity gives a concrete, transferable identity interest the screen can reason about, rooted in Haelan v Topps which first named it
pros.example: Haelan recognized a ball-player's assignable 'right of publicity' in his photograph for trading cards

cons.claim: The right is unevenly recognized and its commercial/expressive boundary is contested, so a single rule over-claims
cons.example: a use that merely references a celebrity in commentary may not be appropriation at all

failure_modes: expressive use mis-treated as commercial appropriation
appropriation found absent any identifiable person
acceptance_tests: a commercial-appropriation theory is stated and tied to an identifiable person and a commercial use
revisit_triggers: NIL appropriation doctrine changes
an endorsement-implication call is disputed

nodes.definition: Treat a person's distinctive voice as a protectable element of identity: deliberately imitating or cloning a recognizable voice to sell or anchor a product can violate publicity/identity rights even when no actual recording is used and no name appears.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: voice-cloning statutes or sound-alike doctrine change

pros.claim: Midler v Ford and Waits v Frito-Lay establish that imitating a distinctive voice to sell a product is actionable misappropriation of identity, independent of copyright
pros.example: Ford hired a Midler sound-alike after she declined; the deliberate imitation of her distinctive voice was actionable

cons.claim: Distinguishing protected distinctive voice from unprotectable style or genre imitation is fact-intensive and jurisdiction-bound
cons.example: a raspy-blues delivery may be a genre convention rather than one singer's protectable signature

failure_modes: synthetic voice clone treated as unprotected because 'no recording was copied'
generic style imitation mis-flagged as protected-voice misappropriation
acceptance_tests: any deliberate recognizable-voice imitation or clone is flagged as a voice-identity risk, not dismissed as 'no recording used'
revisit_triggers: a voice-cloning statute (e.g. Tennessee ELVIS Act) is enacted or amended
a sound-alike call is disputed

nodes.definition: Classify how the figure's likeness is reproduced along the photoreal-to-caricature axis, because the reproduction mode (near-photoreal deepfake, stylized portrait, caricature, or abstract evocation) drives both the strength of the identity claim and the availability of expressive exceptions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: likeness-reproduction taxonomy or deepfake standards change

pros.claim: Separating photoreal reproduction from caricature lets the screen weight a near-perfect deepfake as a strong identity claim while leaving room for transformative caricature
pros.example: a photoreal AI face-swap is a far stronger NIL claim than a recognizable political caricature

cons.claim: The photoreal/caricature line does not by itself decide legality; a transformative caricature can still be commercial appropriation
cons.example: a caricature on merchandise can still appropriate identity for commercial gain

failure_modes: photoreal deepfake under-weighted as 'just a stylization'
caricature assumed automatically lawful regardless of commercial use
acceptance_tests: the reproduction mode is recorded and its identity-claim strength is scored, not assumed lawful from style alone
revisit_triggers: deepfake detection or likeness taxonomy changes
a photoreal reproduction is mis-classified as caricature

nodes.definition: Classify the use as commercial (advertising, endorsement, merchandise), editorial/newsworthy (reporting, commentary, biography), or parody/expressive, because publicity liability turns heavily on this axis and most protective doctrine is anchored to a commercial use.

pros.claim: Classifying use first lets the screen route a pure news report away from appropriation while keeping a thin 'editorial' label from laundering an ad
pros.example: a magazine profile is editorial, but the same image on a product box is commercial regardless of an article wrapper

cons.claim: Modern uses are hybrid (branded content, influencer posts) so a clean three-way label can misroute a mixed use
cons.example: a sponsored 'editorial' video is simultaneously news-styled and an advertisement

failure_modes: an advertisement disguised as editorial routed as protected news
genuine commentary mis-routed as commercial appropriation
acceptance_tests: a defensible use class (commercial / editorial / parody / hybrid) is recorded with the dominant-purpose rationale
revisit_triggers: commercial-speech doctrine shifts
a hybrid sponsored use is mis-classified

nodes.definition: Require documented, scope-matched consent or another lawful basis for any use that implicates identity, voice, or likeness; for voice clones and biometric processing the consent must be specific, informed, and cover the actual use, term, and territory rather than a generic release.

included: lawful-basis record where consent is absent
excluded: whether a use needs consent at all (that is the rights analysis)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: consent / lawful-basis requirements for biometric or voice data change

pros.claim: Demanding scope-matched consent turns 'we have a release' into a checkable artifact and blocks scope-creep voice cloning
pros.example: a stock-photo model release does not authorize generating a synthetic voice clone of that model for an ad

cons.claim: Consent can be defective (coerced, expired, out-of-scope, or from the wrong rights-holder) yet look valid on its face
cons.example: a release signed for a print campaign is silently stretched to cover an AI avatar

failure_modes: generic release treated as voice-clone consent
consent from a non-rights-holder accepted
expired or out-of-territory consent honored
acceptance_tests: a consent/lawful-basis record exists that matches the actual use, voice-clone status, term, and territory, or the use is constrained/blocked
revisit_triggers: biometric/voice consent law changes
a release is found to be out-of-scope for the actual use

nodes.definition: Account for the absence of a uniform US federal right of publicity: protection is state-law-based and materially differs (California Civ. Code 3344 and common law, New York Civil Rights Law 50/51, Tennessee's personal-rights and ELVIS Act regime), so the governing state and its specific scope must be identified.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a state publicity statute is enacted or amended

pros.claim: Explicitly resolving the governing state prevents applying a permissive state's rule to a use governed by a protective one
pros.example: New York 50/51 (image/voice, living persons) differs sharply from Tennessee's broad, descendible, voice-clone-aware regime

cons.claim: Multi-state distribution and online publication make a single governing state hard to pin down, inviting forum uncertainty
cons.example: a clip published nationwide implicates many states' rights at once

failure_modes: a permissive state's rule applied to a use governed by a stricter state
online nationwide use treated as single-state
acceptance_tests: the governing US state(s) and the specific statutory/common-law scope applied are recorded
revisit_triggers: a state publicity statute changes
a multi-state use is collapsed to one state in error

nodes.definition: Account for India's rapidly developing personality-rights regime, where High Courts have granted injunctions protecting a celebrity's name, image, voice, and persona against unauthorized commercial and AI-generated exploitation, so an Indian-facing use of a recognizable persona carries real injunction risk.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new Indian personality-rights judgment or statute issues

pros.claim: Anil Kapoor v Simply Life India (Delhi HC 2023) and DM Entertainment v Baby Gift House show Indian courts will enjoin unauthorized persona and AI exploitation, including voice and likeness
pros.example: Anil Kapoor's suit secured an injunction protecting his name, image, voice, and signature catchphrase against AI/deepfake misuse

cons.claim: Indian personality rights are judge-developed and still evolving, so scope and durability vary case to case
cons.example: the contours of post-mortem and persona protection remain unsettled across High Courts

failure_modes: Indian-facing use of a recognizable persona screened under a permissive foreign standard
emerging Indian AI-persona protection ignored
acceptance_tests: for India-facing uses, the persona/voice protection and injunction risk are assessed against current Indian case law
revisit_triggers: a new Indian personality-rights judgment issues
an Indian-facing AI-persona use is under-screened

nodes.definition: Account for the EU/GDPR layer: a person's image and voice can be personal data, and a voice clone or face model can constitute biometric data (a special category under Art. 9) whose processing needs an explicit lawful basis, independent of any publicity right.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GDPR biometric guidance or national image-rights law changes

pros.claim: Treating a face/voice model as Art. 9 biometric data adds a consent/lawful-basis requirement that publicity law alone would miss for EU-facing uses
pros.example: training a voice clone on an EU resident's recordings processes special-category biometric data needing an explicit basis

cons.claim: Not every image or voice use is biometric processing, and lawful bases beyond consent exist, so a blanket 'GDPR blocks it' over-claims
cons.example: using a photo for editorial reporting may rest on a different lawful basis than consent

failure_modes: EU-facing voice clone processed with no Art. 9 basis
ordinary image use mis-labeled as biometric processing
acceptance_tests: for EU-facing uses, image/voice and any biometric processing are checked for an explicit lawful basis
revisit_triggers: GDPR biometric guidance changes
an EU voice-clone use lacks a recorded lawful basis

nodes.definition: Resolve post-mortem publicity: in several jurisdictions the right survives death and is descendible for a statutory term (e.g. California 70 years, Tennessee renewable terms protecting Elvis-era estates), while elsewhere it dies with the person, so a deceased figure is not automatically free to use.

included: survival and descendibility of the right
excluded: EU data-protection (rights largely end at death)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a post-mortem term or descendibility rule changes

pros.claim: Post-mortem analysis stops the screen from auto-clearing dead celebrities whose estates still control publicity for decades
pros.example: California's statutory post-mortem right and Tennessee's regime keep Elvis-era and similar personas protected long after death

cons.claim: Post-mortem rules vary wildly by jurisdiction and term, so a single answer about 'is the dead person free' is unsafe
cons.example: a figure may be protected in California or Tennessee but free to use under a state where the right dies with the person

failure_modes: deceased figure auto-cleared as unprotected
wrong rights-holder/estate assumed to hold post-mortem rights
acceptance_tests: for a deceased figure, descendibility and the post-mortem term in the governing jurisdiction are resolved before any clearance
revisit_triggers: a post-mortem statutory term changes
a dead-celebrity use is auto-cleared in error

nodes.definition: Evaluate parody, news, and transformative-use exceptions as jurisdiction-specific and fact-bound defenses, NOT automatic safe harbors: tests such as California's transformative-use test and newsworthiness can defeat a publicity claim, but they must be argued, not assumed, and they vary by forum.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: transformative-use or newsworthiness test is revised

pros.claim: Framing exceptions as defenses-to-be-argued prevents the screen from rubber-stamping any 'it's parody' claim as automatic clearance
pros.example: California's transformative-use test asks whether the work adds significant creative expression beyond the likeness, not merely whether it is labeled parody

cons.claim: Exception tests are notoriously indeterminate and forum-dependent, so over-relying on them produces false clearances
cons.example: the same caricature can be transformative in one circuit's test and infringing under another's predominant-purpose test

failure_modes: a labeled 'parody' auto-cleared without an exception analysis
a valid newsworthy use over-blocked by ignoring the defense
acceptance_tests: any claimed exception is recorded as a fact-specific defense with the governing test, never as an automatic safe harbor
revisit_triggers: a transformative-use/newsworthiness precedent changes
a 'parody' label is treated as automatic clearance

nodes.definition: Apply a hard block for minors and other protected/vulnerable persons: any voice clone, deepfake, or commercial likeness use depicting a minor (or a non-consenting protected individual) is blocked and escalated outright, never merely constrained, given heightened consent, child-protection, and biometric concerns.

excluded: exception/parody analysis (does not unblock a minor)

pros.claim: A non-negotiable block for minors fails safe on the highest-harm cases where no commercial or expressive interest can outweigh child protection
pros.example: an AI voice clone or deepface of an identifiable child is blocked outright regardless of any release

cons.claim: Age or protected-status signals can be uncertain at intake, risking either over-blocking adults or under-detecting minors
cons.example: a borderline-age figure may be ambiguous from the artifact alone

failure_modes: minor depiction passed through as a normal commercial balancing case
protected-status signal ignored because consent paperwork was present
acceptance_tests: any minor or protected-person depiction is blocked and escalated, never constrained or auto-approved
revisit_triggers: child-protection rules change
an ambiguous-age subject is processed without escalation

nodes.definition: Apply a hard gate specifically for synthetic voice clones: a recognizable voice clone of a real person for commercial use requires explicit, specific voice-cloning consent (or a clear statutory basis); absent that, the use is blocked, because voice-clone statutes (e.g. Tennessee ELVIS Act 2024) treat unconsented commercial voice cloning as a direct violation.

included: synthetic voice clone of a real person
excluded: adult-only assumption (minors go to the minor gate)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: voice-cloning statute scope or consent standard changes

pros.claim: Tennessee's ELVIS Act 2024 makes a person's voice a protected property right and targets unconsented AI voice cloning, so a clone-specific consent gate matches the live statutory direction
pros.example: the ELVIS Act extended Tennessee's right of publicity to expressly cover a person's voice and unauthorized simulation

cons.claim: Voice-clone statutes are new, uneven across jurisdictions, and their commercial/expressive carve-outs are still being litigated
cons.example: a clone used in a clearly expressive, non-commercial work may fall outside some statutes

failure_modes: unconsented commercial voice clone passed as 'no recording copied'
clone-specific consent conflated with a generic likeness release
acceptance_tests: a recognizable commercial voice clone without explicit voice-clone consent or statutory basis is blocked and escalated
revisit_triggers: a voice-cloning statute is enacted or amended
a clone is cleared on a generic likeness release

nodes.definition: Set the default posture to fail-closed: when identifiability, consent, jurisdiction, or exception signals are missing, conflicting, or low-confidence, the screen must NOT auto-approve; it defaults to constrain, block, or human-review rather than allow.

excluded: the substantive merits decision (that is the verdict map)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: risk tolerance or default-posture policy changes

pros.claim: A fail-closed default guarantees that an incomplete or ambiguous screen never silently green-lights an identity use
pros.example: a tuple missing jurisdiction and consent resolves to human-review, not allow

cons.claim: Aggressive fail-closed defaults raise false-positive blocks that frustrate clearly lawful uses and create review load
cons.example: a plainly newsworthy use may be needlessly routed to review under a strict default

failure_modes: uncertainty resolved toward allow
a missing-consent case auto-approved on weak signals
acceptance_tests: with any missing/conflicting/low-confidence signal, the screen never outputs allow; it constrains, blocks, or routes to human-review
revisit_triggers: risk-tolerance policy changes
an auto-approve on incomplete signals is observed

nodes.definition: Map the assembled signals for an (item, figure, use) tuple to a disposition in {allow, constrain, block, human-review}, where allow is reserved for clearly lawful or fully consented uses, constrain attaches conditions, block stops disallowed identity uses, and human-review routes the genuinely uncertain.

excluded: auto-approving without a consent or clear-lawfulness basis

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: verdict taxonomy or disposition criteria change

pros.claim: A four-way disposition with allow reserved for clear/consented cases gives a deterministic, auditable output while preserving the no-auto-approve and hard-block invariants
pros.example: a fully consented adult endorsement maps to allow; an unconsented voice clone maps to block; a hybrid sponsored use maps to human-review

cons.claim: Compressing a nuanced legal posture into four buckets can over- or under-call borderline uses, so the map must defer rather than guess
cons.example: a novel transformative-AI use may not fit cleanly and should route to review, not a confident allow

failure_modes: a hard-gate case mapped to allow/constrain instead of block
a genuinely uncertain case forced to a confident verdict
acceptance_tests: every tuple maps to exactly one disposition; hard gates force block; uncertainty forces human-review; allow requires a consent or clear-lawfulness basis
revisit_triggers: disposition criteria change
a hard-gate case is mis-mapped to allow

nodes.definition: Define the escalation heuristic that routes any block, hard-gate trigger, or human-review disposition to qualified legal counsel for an actual legal determination, making clear the screen is a triage signal and the binding decision belongs to counsel.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: escalation routing or counsel-engagement policy changes

pros.claim: Explicit escalation to counsel keeps the screen as a triage tool and ensures high-risk and blocked tuples reach a qualified human decision-maker
pros.example: every minor, voice-clone-without-consent, and block disposition is routed to counsel with its rationale

cons.claim: Over-escalation can overwhelm counsel and erode the triage value, so the trigger set must be calibrated to genuine risk
cons.example: routing every editorial mention to counsel would swamp the queue and defeat triage

failure_modes: a high-risk block not escalated to counsel
escalation used as a substitute for, rather than a route to, a legal determination
acceptance_tests: every block, hard-gate trigger, and human-review disposition is routed to qualified counsel with its rationale recorded
revisit_triggers: escalation policy changes
a blocked tuple is closed without counsel review

nodes.definition: Record the provenance of each screening decision: the input tuple, every rule/right/jurisdiction signal that fired, the consent artifact relied on (if any), and the resulting disposition, so a decision is reconstructable and reviewable.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: provenance schema or audit requirements change

pros.claim: A provenance record turns each disposition into an auditable artifact counsel and reviewers can reconstruct
pros.example: 'why was this blocked?' is answered by the logged voice-clone gate trigger and absent consent

cons.claim: Full provenance carries storage and privacy overhead, and logging identity signals itself processes personal data needing care
cons.example: logging a face/voice signal is itself biometric data handling

failure_modes: disposition recorded without the signals that produced it
provenance log itself mishandles the identity data it stores
acceptance_tests: every disposition stores the tuple, fired signals, consent reference, and outcome in a reconstructable record
revisit_triggers: provenance schema changes
a disposition cannot be reconstructed for review

nodes.definition: Audit the screen for calibration and for two non-negotiable invariants: it never issues legal advice and never auto-approves; periodically sample dispositions against counsel outcomes to detect drift, over-blocking, or any auto-approve regression, and surface the screening disclaimer on every output.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: audit policy, disclaimer wording, or calibration target changes

pros.claim: A standing audit of the two invariants catches drift and any regression toward auto-approval before it causes harm, and keeps the disclaimer visible
pros.example: a sampled batch reveals over-blocking of newsworthy uses, prompting a calibration fix without weakening the hard gates

cons.claim: Audit signal lags real outcomes, so a rare auto-approve or advice-like output can slip between sampling windows
cons.example: a single mis-phrased output reading as legal advice may pass until the next audit

failure_modes: an auto-approve regression undetected between audits
disclaimer dropped from some output paths
acceptance_tests: the audit confirms zero auto-approvals, no legal-advice outputs, and a calibrated disposition mix, with the disclaimer present on every output
revisit_triggers: audit policy changes
a missed auto-approve or advice-like output is found

edges.why_related: India-facing injunction risk constrains the admissible disposition for a recognizable persona
an absent Art. 9 biometric basis constrains an EU-facing use toward constrain/block
a surviving post-mortem right blocks auto-clearing a deceased figure in the verdict map
a minor signal forces the fail-closed posture to a hard block rather than a constrain
unresolved identifiability is a missing signal that triggers the fail-closed default
escalation attaches its rationale to the provenance record handed to counsel
audit findings of over-blocking or drift feed back to recalibrate the verdict map
audit detection of an auto-approve regression feeds back to harden the fail-closed default
the parody/transformative defense pulls toward allow while the right of publicity pulls toward block
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: the expressive defense never auto-clears: apply the governing transformative-use/newsworthiness test as a fact-specific defense; if it is not clearly met, the publicity right controls and the use is constrained, blocked, or escalated

edges.why_related: an editorial/newsworthy classification pulls toward allow while fail-closed pulls hybrid uses toward review
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: a clean 'editorial' label does not override fail-closed: when use class is hybrid or low-confidence, the fail-closed default routes to human-review rather than honoring the editorial label as allow

edges.why_related: the verdict map may lean allow on other signals while the voice-clone gate forces block
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: the voice-clone hard gate dominates the verdict map: an unconsented commercial voice clone is forced to block regardless of other allow-leaning signals, and escalated to counsel

edges.why_related: a US-style transformative defense pulls toward allow while India's persona-rights regime pulls an India-facing use toward block
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: do not import a foreign expressive exception into an India-facing use: assess the exception only under the governing forum's law, and where India's persona-injunction risk applies, the exception does not auto-clear it

conflict_axes.name: identity_protection_vs_free_expression
conflict_axes.description: Protecting an identifiable persona guards against appropriation but can over-restrict legitimate expression, commentary, and parody.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: weight a commercial use toward protection and an expressive/newsworthy use toward expression, but argue, do not assume, the exception

conflict_axes.name: voice_as_identity_vs_style_imitation
conflict_axes.description: A distinctive voice is protectable identity, but unprotectable genre or style imitation lies close by; over-protecting chills lawful homage, under-protecting permits sound-alike misappropriation.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: flag deliberate recognizable-voice imitation/clone; treat generic genre style as style, and escalate the borderline

conflict_axes.name: commercial_use_vs_editorial_newsworthy
conflict_axes.description: Commercial appropriation is the core wrong, but an editorial/newsworthy label can both legitimately protect reporting and be misused to launder an advertisement.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: classify by dominant purpose; route hybrid/sponsored uses to human-review

conflict_axes.name: consent_presence_vs_consent_scope
conflict_axes.description: A signed release may exist yet not cover the actual use, term, territory, or voice-clone status; presence is not scope.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: validate scope, term, territory, and clone-specificity, not mere presence of a release

conflict_axes.name: jurisdictional_divergence_vs_single_rule
conflict_axes.description: No uniform federal right and divergent state, Indian, and EU regimes mean one rule misapplies; resolving the governing forum is unavoidable but hard for multi-jurisdiction publication.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: resolve the governing forum per audience; apply the strictest applicable regime when ambiguous

conflict_axes.name: post_mortem_protection_vs_public_domain_persona
conflict_axes.description: A deceased figure's persona may still be a descendible asset for decades or may have entered free use, depending entirely on jurisdiction and term.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: resolve descendibility and term in the governing jurisdiction before any clearance

conflict_axes.name: fail_closed_safety_vs_false_positive_blocks
conflict_axes.description: A strict fail-closed default prevents silent green-lighting but raises false-positive blocks and review load for clearly lawful uses.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep no-auto-approve absolute; calibrate the constrain/review threshold via the audit loop

conflict_axes.name: exception_availability_vs_indeterminacy
conflict_axes.description: Expressive exceptions can defeat a publicity claim but are forum-dependent and indeterminate, so relying on them risks false clearances.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat any exception as a defense to be argued; escalate indeterminate ones rather than auto-clearing

conflict_axes.name: automation_triage_vs_legal_determination
conflict_axes.description: The screen adds value as fast triage but must never substitute for a qualified legal determination or issue legal advice.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: emit a non-binding disposition plus disclaimer; route every block/hard-gate/review to counsel

edge_cases.description: An AI voice clone of a named singer is used in an ad with no actual recording copied, asserted as 'no copyright issue'.
edge_cases.trigger: synthetic voice clone for commercial use without explicit voice-clone consent
edge_cases.mitigation: flag voice-identity misappropriation (Midler/Waits) and block under the voice-clone gate absent explicit consent

edge_cases.description: A photoreal deepfake of a living celebrity endorses a product under a generic stock-model release.
edge_cases.trigger: out-of-scope release stretched to cover a synthetic deepfake endorsement
edge_cases.mitigation: reject the generic release as not scope-matched; block and escalate

edge_cases.description: A robot or look-alike posed as a celebrity evokes them without name, image, or voice.
edge_cases.trigger: evocation of a distinctive persona with no literal name/face/voice
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the identifiability-by-evocation standard (White v Samsung, Wendt) rather than dismissing for lack of a literal name

edge_cases.description: An identifiable minor is depicted in an AI-generated likeness or voice clone for a commercial use.
edge_cases.trigger: minor or protected-person subject reaches the screen
edge_cases.mitigation: hard-block and escalate outright regardless of any release; never constrain or auto-approve

edge_cases.description: A deceased celebrity's persona is used commercially, assumed free because the person has died.
edge_cases.trigger: deceased figure auto-treated as public domain
edge_cases.mitigation: resolve descendibility and the post-mortem term (e.g. California, Tennessee) before any clearance

edge_cases.description: A use of an Indian celebrity's AI-generated persona is screened only under a permissive foreign standard.
edge_cases.trigger: India-facing recognizable-persona use screened under non-Indian law
edge_cases.mitigation: assess India personality-rights injunction risk (Anil Kapoor v Simply Life) for India-facing uses

edge_cases.description: An EU-facing voice clone is trained on a resident's recordings with no Art. 9 lawful basis.
edge_cases.trigger: biometric (voice model) processing of an EU data subject without an explicit basis
edge_cases.mitigation: require an explicit GDPR Art. 9 basis; block/constrain the EU-facing use absent one

edge_cases.description: A sponsored 'editorial' video is both news-styled and an advertisement and is routed as protected news.
edge_cases.trigger: hybrid commercial/editorial use mis-classified as pure editorial
edge_cases.mitigation: classify by dominant purpose; route hybrid sponsored uses to human-review, not allow

edge_cases.description: A caricature is labeled 'parody' and treated as automatically cleared regardless of commercial sale.
edge_cases.trigger: parody label asserted as an automatic safe harbor
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the governing transformative-use test as a fact-specific defense; do not auto-clear on the label

edge_cases.description: A tuple arrives with no asserted jurisdiction and an ambiguous figure, yet a disposition is demanded.
edge_cases.trigger: missing jurisdiction and weak identifiability signals
edge_cases.mitigation: fail closed: route to human-review rather than allow on incomplete signals

edge_cases.description: The screen produces a confident 'allow' on a borderline use, reading like a legal clearance.
edge_cases.trigger: a borderline use auto-approved and phrased as legal advice
edge_cases.mitigation: enforce no-auto-approve and no-legal-advice invariants; surface the disclaimer and route to counsel

edge_cases.description: Over time the screen drifts toward over-blocking clearly newsworthy uses, eroding trust in triage.
edge_cases.trigger: calibration drift detected against counsel outcomes
edge_cases.mitigation: use the audit loop to recalibrate the constrain/review threshold without weakening hard gates

workflow.description: Normalize the screening unit into an (item, figure, use) tuple with asserted jurisdiction(s).
workflow.gate: tuple has a figure, a concrete use, and at least one jurisdiction

workflow.description: Determine whether a real, identifiable person is depicted or evoked and record the identifiability theory.
workflow.gate: an identifiability theory (name/image/voice/persona) is recorded or the figure is dropped

workflow.description: State the commercial-appropriation theory tying the identifiable person to the commercial use.
workflow.gate: a commercial-appropriation theory is stated or explicitly absent

workflow.description: Assess distinctive-voice imitation/clone and the likeness reproduction mode.
workflow.gate: any deliberate voice clone or photoreal likeness is flagged

workflow.description: Classify the use as commercial, editorial/newsworthy, parody, or hybrid by dominant purpose.
workflow.gate: a use class with dominant-purpose rationale is recorded

workflow.description: Verify scope-matched consent or another lawful basis, including explicit voice-clone authorization.
workflow.gate: consent/basis matches actual use/term/territory or the use is constrained/blocked

workflow.description: Resolve the governing US state and any India/EU/post-mortem overlay for the audience.
workflow.gate: the governing regime(s) and their scope are recorded

workflow.description: Evaluate any claimed expressive/newsworthy exception as a fact-bound defense under the governing test.
workflow.gate: any exception is recorded as a defense with its test, never as automatic clearance

workflow.description: Apply the minor/protected-person and unconsented voice-clone hard blocks.
workflow.gate: any minor or unconsented commercial voice clone is blocked and escalated

workflow.description: On any missing/conflicting/low-confidence signal, default to constrain/block/human-review, never allow.
workflow.gate: no allow is emitted on incomplete or conflicting signals

workflow.description: Map the assembled signals to exactly one of allow/constrain/block/human-review with hard gates overriding.
workflow.gate: exactly one disposition; allow requires a consent or clear-lawfulness basis

workflow.description: Route every block/hard-gate/human-review disposition to qualified counsel; log provenance and audit the invariants.
workflow.gate: high-risk dispositions reach counsel; disclaimer surfaced; no auto-approve or legal-advice output

priority_rationale: intake and identifiability are foundational; the right-of-publicity, voice, likeness, classification, and consent units build the substantive screen; jurisdiction and exception overlays refine it; the minor and voice-clone hard gates plus the fail-closed default dominate; the verdict map, counsel escalation, provenance, and audit close the fail-closed legal gate last.

dominance_rules.rule: MINOR_PROTECTION blocks and escalates any minor or protected-person depiction regardless of consent, exception, or commercial value
dominance_rules.rationale: child protection and heightened consent concerns outweigh any commercial or expressive interest
dominance_rules.trigger: a minor or protected-person subject is detected
dominance_rules.action: hard-block and escalate; never constrain or allow

dominance_rules.rule: VOICE_CLONE_CONSENT_GATE blocks any unconsented recognizable commercial voice clone regardless of allow-leaning signals
dominance_rules.rationale: voice-clone statutes (ELVIS Act) treat unconsented commercial cloning as a direct violation
dominance_rules.trigger: a commercial voice clone lacks explicit voice-clone consent or statutory basis
dominance_rules.action: force block and escalate to counsel

dominance_rules.rule: FAIL_CLOSED_DEFAULT prohibits any allow output when identifiability, consent, jurisdiction, or exception signals are missing or conflicting
dominance_rules.rationale: the screen must never silently green-light an identity use on incomplete information
dominance_rules.trigger: a required signal is missing, conflicting, or low-confidence

dominance_rules.rule: The legal gate dominates: no exception, business value, or throughput pressure may convert a block or hard-gate trigger into an allow
dominance_rules.rationale: the screen is a fail-closed legal gate; identity-protection and statutory blocks take precedence over convenience
dominance_rules.trigger: an allow is proposed over an active block or hard-gate trigger
dominance_rules.action: reject the allow and uphold the block

dominance_rules.rule: PARODY_TRANSFORMATIVE_EXCEPTION may never auto-clear; an unmet or indeterminate exception leaves the publicity right controlling
dominance_rules.rationale: expressive exceptions are fact-bound, forum-dependent defenses, not safe harbors
dominance_rules.trigger: a parody/transformative label is asserted as automatic clearance
dominance_rules.action: require the governing test be met or escalate; otherwise the right controls

dominance_rules.rule: CONSENT_LICENSE requires scope-matched consent; a generic or out-of-scope release does not authorize the use
dominance_rules.rationale: presence of a release is not coverage of the actual use, term, territory, or clone status
dominance_rules.trigger: a release is offered that does not match the actual use
dominance_rules.action: treat as unconsented; constrain or block

dominance_rules.rule: For multi-jurisdiction publication, apply the strictest applicable regime when the governing forum is ambiguous
dominance_rules.rationale: divergent regimes mean a permissive rule must not be applied to a use governed by a stricter one
dominance_rules.trigger: the governing forum cannot be uniquely resolved
dominance_rules.action: apply the strictest applicable regime or escalate

dominance_rules.rule: POST_MORTEM_RIGHTS must be resolved before any deceased figure is cleared
dominance_rules.rationale: descendible publicity can protect a persona for decades after death in some jurisdictions
dominance_rules.trigger: a deceased figure is proposed for clearance
dominance_rules.action: resolve descendibility and term first; do not auto-clear

dominance_rules.rule: VERDICT_MAP must emit exactly one disposition and reserve allow for clearly lawful or fully consented uses
dominance_rules.rationale: a deterministic, auditable output preserves the no-auto-approve and hard-block invariants
dominance_rules.action: emit one of allow/constrain/block/human-review with allow gated on consent or clear lawfulness

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not screen a tuple before the figure's identifiability is resolved; an unidentified figure invalidates every downstream right test
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-running rights, jurisdiction, and consent analysis after the figure is finally identified

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not accept a generic release as consent; validate scope/term/territory/clone-status up front
anti_rework_rules.prevents: clearing a use on a release that is later found out-of-scope, forcing a recall

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not apply a single jurisdiction's rule before resolving the governing forum for the actual audience
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-screening under the correct regime after applying a permissive state's rule in error

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not auto-clear a deceased figure; resolve post-mortem descendibility before clearance
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recalling a 'cleared' use of a still-protected estate persona

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not treat a parody/transformative or newsworthiness label as automatic clearance; record it as a defense to be argued
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reversing a false clearance after the exception fails under the governing test

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not emit an allow on incomplete or conflicting signals; fail closed to human-review first
anti_rework_rules.prevents: retracting an auto-approval that should have been a review or block

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not let any disposition skip the hard gates; minors and unconsented voice clones must block before the verdict map
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rework when a hard-gate case is discovered to have been allowed or constrained

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not close a disposition without provenance and disclaimer; missing records force re-screening for counsel and audit
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reconstructing a decision from scratch when counsel or the audit cannot trace it

iteration_protocol.trigger: an unconsented voice clone is found to have passed as 'no recording copied'
iteration_protocol.action: tighten the voice-clone gate in VOICE_CLONE_CONSENT_GATE and re-evaluate VOICE_PROTECTION flagging

iteration_protocol.trigger: a minor or protected-person depiction is processed without a hard block
iteration_protocol.action: audit the MINOR_PROTECTION trigger and the FAIL_CLOSED_DEFAULT routing for that path

iteration_protocol.trigger: an auto-approve or legal-advice-like output is detected in the audit
iteration_protocol.action: harden the no-auto-approve invariant in FAIL_CLOSED_DEFAULT and VERDICT_MAP and re-surface the disclaimer in DECISION_AUDIT

iteration_protocol.trigger: a use governed by a stricter forum was screened under a permissive one
iteration_protocol.action: refine forum resolution in US_STATE_BY_STATE and the overlays in INDIA_PERSONALITY_RIGHTS and EU_BIOMETRIC_BASIS

iteration_protocol.trigger: a deceased figure was auto-cleared as public domain
iteration_protocol.action: re-run POST_MORTEM_RIGHTS descendibility and add the term check before clearance in VERDICT_MAP

iteration_protocol.trigger: a parody/transformative label was treated as automatic clearance
iteration_protocol.action: reassert the no-auto-clear rule in PARODY_TRANSFORMATIVE_EXCEPTION and route the borderline to ESCALATE_TO_COUNSEL

iteration_protocol.trigger: a generic release was accepted as scope-matched consent
iteration_protocol.action: tighten scope/term/territory validation in CONSENT_LICENSE and the clone-specific check in VOICE_CLONE_CONSENT_GATE

iteration_protocol.trigger: the audit shows calibration drift toward over-blocking newsworthy uses
iteration_protocol.action: recalibrate the constrain/review threshold in VERDICT_MAP via DECISION_AUDIT without weakening the hard gates

required_checks: all edge ids unique EDGE_XXX format
all from/to in edges reference valid node ids

all evidence_refs resolve to valid source_registry ids
all priority_order entries are valid node ids with no duplicates
high_risk_nodes (risk_if_wrong>=0.80) have non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true
conflict edges have signed_tension<0 and resolution_rule present
observed_impact=0.0 for all nodes (no observed data)
19-24 nodes, 32-40 edges, 8-10 conflict_axes, 10-12 edge_cases, 9-12 workflow steps
